rationale: AFTER-REVEAL REVIEW, not a blind trial result. The earlier altered-card review remains separate and unchanged. I verified genuine card file SHA256 0f3fb77547b3446f985d36ba2e649e2bc1aa05228484d1d4fdf4c5ab632e0dce and its canonical compact sorted-key UTF-8 claim SHA256 6b72d9131bcf9cb465fde497c35e4870501f85ba931255f24beb4d1a4c961c7a. I re-opened and visually re-read the original PDF p. 45, printed p. 816, already rendered from source PDF whose SHA256 was independently verified as 3bce4d490526a69516217faf43b66b62adf565a388b622f6d1e9225faffdcdf5. EO 5595 is the complete separate instrument beginning 'Executive Order 5595. April 9, 1931' and ending [No. 5595]; the land provisions above belong to EO 5594 and cannot be treated as residual directions of this order. The sole operative paragraph orders flags on the White House and public buildings in the District of Columbia and the State of Ohio to 'be placed at half mast to-day and on the day of the funeral service at Cincinnati, Ohio, Saturday, April 11, 1931.' All named flags and both prescribed occasions are covered by the claim. 'To-day' is April 9, the signing date. The April 11 requirement remains prospective after the April 9 occasion; neither an April 9 placement nor the intervening April 10 exhausts the complete instruction. Because the final specified civil day is April 11, April 12, 1931 is the first civil date after the entire prescribed temporal scope has ended. This supports 1931-04-12 as the first-inoperative date under a next-civil-day representation, rather than a claim that the text expressly prints April 12 or fixes a precise hour. The funeral wording identifies the second prescribed day and does not create a separate continuing funeral administration duty. No recurrence, reporting, appropriation, payment, personnel power, delegated authority, institution, savings clause or other surviving legal command appears between heading and closing number. Historical mourning and any consequences of compliance or noncompliance do not extend the prescribed flag occasions. The substantive quotation is faithful to the image apart from OCR formatting. No earlier terminating condition appears in this original. Material limits: the original does not prove actual flag performance, a particular hour of last operation on April 11, or the absence of an external intervening amendment or revocation. I have not independently repeated the card's reported later-source searches, and their disclosed pre-1937 and current-law coverage limits remain. With those limits, the whole-case own-terms conclusion and April 12 first-inoperative civil date are upheld. No private key, producer packet, or other reviewer's analysis was consulted.
